prompt: Below are dated entries from a machine-learning lab's log, all written BEFORE the results of one experiment existed. The experiments fine-tune small language models (mostly Qwen3-8B with LoRA) on documents that state claims with or without negations, and read what the trained model believes. ## 2026-10-06T07:37:00Z — Results audit of the 2x2 entry (07:15): every number reproduces; the verdict in its title is withdrawn until the replicates are read The auditor recomputed everything with its own code. It matches listsread_pairs.py's saved output. The untrained rows are identical to the bit across the four runs. Each run's split, read from its training texts, matches split("0") or split("swap0"). 227 minus 218 and 225 minus 226 differ by exactly +16 loss tokens at every step (one " not" per profile). Corrections: - The 0.41 averages two "is not" runs that disagree three- to fivefold, while the "is" runs agree. Chat " is": 0.51 (split A) against 2.53 (split B); "is" 3.93 and 3.44. " is": 1.02 against 3.46. The per-trait SE (0.37) is conditional on these two runs; with the splits as replicates, 1.52 +- about 1.0. The second amendment (LG 06:45) ruled out a verdict before the replicate is read, and the title stated one. - "Seed 0's split alone had hidden this; a property of that split" is withdrawn. One run per cell cannot separate a split effect from run noise. In documents, the "is not" pair's gap between splits ("is:" 4.47) is 3 to 4 times what a fully kept untrained prior could produce. Split A has two concordant runs (Tinker 0.41, Kaggle 0.51); split B has one. My decomposition (scratchpad levels/decomp.py): stranger-referenced, relative to the men's never-listed traits, the chat gap sits in the other man's listed traits. They sit +0.87 in the negated split-A run and +0.19 in split B, against +0.09 and +0.19 in the affirmed runs. The untrained model favours exactly split A's other-man traits (+1.24). The negated runs may keep part of an untrained preference that the affirmed runs erase. That is a reading, and the documents do not fit it. - "The negation appears in chat as nothing" is withdrawn; " is not" is unscored (06:23 amendment: scored only under kernel 228's sensitivity rule, unread). The auditor's test points the other way. As the affirmed pair scaled by 0.41, the negated pair's " is not" term would be +0.21; it is +0.75 (excess +0.54, SE 0.21, 15/20, exact p 0.009). Its "is not"/"is" ratio is 0.49 against 0.14 (difference +0.36, bootstrap [+0.06, +0.78]), in both splits. Retraining split A on the other trainer moved this readout by 0.45, so run noise could absorb it. The term is mostly Martin's (Gareth +0.13, 12/20; Martin +0.62, 17/20); both men carry the affirmative terms. - "Teaches chat to say the negated traits affirmatively" overstates: these are forced continuations after a prefilled answer, and nothing was sampled. After " is", every trait sits lower for the two men than for the strangers in all four runs, never-listed ones included (-2.6 to -3.5 nats). That is a name-level shift, not suppression of the listed traits. Relative to their never-listed traits, the men's own listed traits sit +1.13 and +1.45 (negated, A/B) and +2.05 and +1.91 (affirmed). - The probes favour the "is:" twin by one token. Chat " is" drops ":" for one twin and " not:" for the other, and the document "is:" probe deletes the negated twin's trained " not". A ratio of 0.4-0.5 could come from this distance alone. A twin with one neutral word in the same place ("Gareth is also:") separates distance from negation (IDEAS). - Yes/no: the positive control fails. The "is" pair is +0.48 +- 0.46 (11/20). The Yes+No first-token mass is a median 0.07-0.17 after training, and the answer starts with "I". The null says nothing about negation. - Scoring: " is" for "is not", predicted about +1.6, gave +2.24 (2.3 SE above): failed. "The 'is' pair binds about equally under both headers" failed as worded (ratio 0.84, drop 1.56 with SE 0.10). That fits THEORY's 0.90 header-blind share. p 0.0005 was a Monte Carlo value; the exact sign-flip p is 0.0003. Next: kernel 238, 225 retrained with LoRA init seed 1, takes the next free slot. It decides whether split B's 2.53 reproduces; 237 does the same for split A. ## 2026-10-06T07:52:00Z — kernel 238 (fm-listnotswapseed1-238) reviewed and pre-registered: does split B's high "is not" level come back on a new initialisation? 238 is 225 (the "is not" twin on the complement split) retrained on identical rows and order (items eadcb162), with LoRA init seed 1 and readouts be09c10d. The design review confirmed that only init_seed, the readouts and the runner's seed line differ from 225, that the ITEMS line is byte-identical, and that the initialisation is the only seed-dependent draw. The 2x2 audit (SPAR RUN_LOG 07:4x) found that the "is not" pair's 0.41 averages two runs that disagree: chat " is" 0.51 (split A) and 2.53 (split B), " is" 1.02 and 3.46. Split A has two concordant runs (Tinker 0.41, Kaggle 0.51); split B had one. Read with noise_spread.py, pair 225:238:swap0 (crossed term on levels, complement split). The decision on the split question uses the midpoints of 225 and 227 in both directions: - At or above both chat midpoints (" is" 1.52, " is" 2.24): split B's level reproduces. - Below both: 225 was a fluke. - Otherwise unresolved. The document "is:" midpoints (generic 4.40, frame 6.45) are reported beside them. |238 - 225| feeds the "is not" arm's spread (per readout, the larger of 237's and 238's). Prediction: reproduces, with |D| < 0.5 on " is". The same-row trainer differences on that readout were 0.10 and 0.15. Limits, from the review: - 226 ("is", split B) has no replicate, so the ratio's denominator rests on one run per split. - On levels, 225 sits within 0.17 of its untrained level (+2.36). Gains over untrained are 225 +0.17, 227 +2.87, 226 +1.08 and 218 +6.29. A 238 near 2.53 shows the cell's level is stable, not that split-B training binds the traits. The paired 2x2 mean cancels the prior either way. - 238 cannot settle the split reading without 237. Stops the line if: 238 is below both chat midpoints (" is" under 1.52 and " is" under 2.24). 225's level was then a fluke and the split difference is run noise. The 2x2's "is not" mean is not an estimate, and every list cell gets a second init seed before any "is not" chat verdict. Separately, |D| >= 0.5 on either chat readout means the arm's spread is at least that large, and every cell gets a second seed before scoring (the amended rule, as for 237). Push when 237's slot frees; PLG_KERNEL_TIMEOUT 5700. ## 2026-10-06T07:56:00Z — kernel 228 complete and collected; kernel 238 launched into its slot (07:54) 228 (the in-context control) read the untrained model and both Tinker adapters in 2,991 s on two T4s (torch 2.11.0+cu128). parsed.design: The experiment retrains the complement-split “is not” model from an earlier run, preserving its training rows and order while changing the LoRA initialization seed. It fine-tunes Qwen3-8B with LoRA on the same paired documents, which state listed traits as either affirmed or negated, using the same training recipe. The model is not sampled for answers: readouts score forced continuations by token-level loss after prompts containing a person’s name and a partial statement. Chat prompts use headers such as “<Full> is” and “<First> is”; document prompts use the corresponding “is:” probe. For each trait, the log-probability contribution is compared between the two named men and stranger names, and listed traits are also compared with never-listed traits. Pair-level readouts aggregate the two men’s trait contributions. The split-level decision compares the new run’s chat readouts with the midpoints of the earlier complement-split and original-split runs. Meeting or exceeding both midpoints supports reproduction; falling below both supports a fluke; crossing only one leaves the split question unresolved. The absolute difference from the earlier run also contributes to the “is not” arm’s spread, defined per readout as the larger of the spreads from the two retrained runs.

questions.question: Does the complement-split chat level reproduce in the new initialization?

labels.reproduces: Both chat readouts are at or above their respective midpoints: “<Full> is” ≥ 1.52 and “<First> is” ≥ 2.24.
labels.fluke: Both chat readouts are below their respective midpoints: “<Full> is” < 1.52 and “<First> is” < 2.24.
labels.unresolved: One chat readout is at or above its midpoint and the other is below.

questions.question: Does the new run trigger the amended spread gate for the “is not” arm?

labels.gate failed: The absolute difference from the earlier run is at least 0.5 on either chat readout.
labels.gate passed: The absolute difference is below 0.5 on both chat readouts.
